item.title: UCTH: Group presses for immediate CMD advert
item.description: …alleges plot to install acting head …Ikpeme dismisses claim as “falsehood” By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR A socio-political group, Good Governance Initiative (GGI), has accused the management of the University of Calabar Teaching Hospital (UCTH) of stalling the recruitment of a new Chief Medical Director (CMD), alleging a scheme to install an acting head and ease in a preferred successor. The Chief Medical Director, Prof. Ikpeme Ikpeme, has rejected the allegation. GGI’s Convener, Mr Bassey Okoi, made the demand in a statement in Calabar on Wednesday, calling for the immediate advertisement of the position, which falls vacant on April 16, 2027, when Ikpeme’s second tenure ends. Okoi said the vacancy should have been advertised in national newspapers six months before the incumbent’s tenure expires. The group had expected the process to start on November 1, he said, but there was no sign of it. He alleged that the delay was meant to tilt the succession in favour of a candidate from Cross River’s southern senatorial district. Okoi insisted that the central senatorial district should produce the next CMD under a long-standing zoning arrangement among the three senatorial districts. He recalled that Prof. Thomas Agan, from the northern district, served eight years before the office moved to the south. According to him, allowing the central district to produce the next CMD is the fairest course, and the incumbent appears determined to disrupt the arrangement. He stressed that zoning was not meant to undermine competence but to promote fairness, inclusiveness and a sense of belonging. He warned that manipulating the process could cause tension and damage institutional harmony. Okoi urged the Federal Ministry of Health to ensure that the recruitment was transparent, credible and consistent with regulations. He also appealed to stakeholders to back an equitable process, saying no individual or interest group should predetermine the outcome. When contacted, Prof. Ikpeme dismissed the claims and said he had already begun the process of appointing his successor ahead of time. He advised the group’s sponsors to stop wasting energy on what he called falsehood and to draw up a programme for taking the hospital to the next level instead. He said the group should take its concerns to the Federal Ministry of Health, the appropriate authority on such appointments. Pointing to the reforms he had carried out to reposition the hospital, Ikpeme said he was no party to the dispute. “I am not a contestant,” he said. item.title: Bayern confirm Musiala’s neurological symptoms began in 2025, pledge recovery support
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala’s management have reaffirmed their support for the midfielder’s recovery and clarified that he was first examined for neurological symptoms on April 22, 2025, immediately after they appeared. In a joint statement after talks on Tuesday, the club and 11WINS, the agency representing Musiala, said: “Both sides agree that the player’s health comes first. Jamal Musiala has their full support on his road to recovery.” Addressing speculation about the midfielder’s health, they added: “Jamal Musiala was first examined for absence-like symptoms on April 22, 2025. This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical department immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared.” The statement said Bayern and Musiala’s management had agreed to continue discussions “in a spirit of partnership and confidentiality”. Musiala has said he was diagnosed with “easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction” after collapsing twice in four days during pre-season. Bayern sporting director Max Eberl described Tuesday’s meeting as “very, very constructive” and said the club’s priority was helping Musiala return after a muscle injury sustained during the international break. “That’s the only task FC Bayern has currently, to give Jamal this trust and not some topics about money or something,” Eberl said. The talks follow debate over the Germany international’s form and his contract, which runs until 2030. Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen had questioned the lucrative extension if Musiala did not return to his best, while former chief executive Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the deal might need to be renegotiated. Players’ union FIFPRO criticised the club’s public comments, saying an injury or dip in form was no reason to reopen agreed contract terms. Honorary president Uli Hoeness had said Musiala might never regain his previous performance level. Musiala has made five appearances this season, scoring twice. item.title: Ughelli Killings: Obidient Movement faults police, urges probe
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Obidient Movement has condemned the November 23 attack on the campaign team of former Deputy President of the Senate and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Delta Central Senatorial candidate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, which reportedly left four persons dead and several others injured. The movement expressed concern over the security situation in the state, accusing the Nigeria Police Force of failing to prevent attacks on political supporters and calling for an independent investigation into the conduct of officers deployed to the campaign ground. In a statement on Wednesday signed by its Director of Media and Communications, Onyeka Dike, the movement urged Nigerians to take their personal security seriously while calling on security agencies to ensure the protection of citizens irrespective of their political affiliations. It alleged that the police had failed to adequately protect opposition supporters during attacks in Delta State and accused some officers of showing bias in their handling of politically related incidents. The movement said it was particularly concerned that armed attackers reportedly operated at the campaign venue despite the presence of several truckloads of police personnel. The statement read, “The Obidient Movement strongly condemns the murderous attack on Senator Ovie Omo-Agege and members of his NDC campaign team in Uduere, Ughelli North, Delta State, by APC thugs on November 23, 2026, which left several people dead and others seriously injured, including outspoken activist, Comrade Efemena Umukoro (Akima) and Senator Omo-Agege’s aide, Comrade Moses Anuaghe.” The movement alleged that the attacks on NDC supporters in Delta State had continued despite the presence of security personnel. “We are particularly outraged by the conduct of the Nigeria Police Force during yesterday’s attack. Six truckloads of policemen were reportedly at the campaign ground, yet they failed to stop armed men from attacking and killing innocent Nigerians. What exactly were they deployed there to do?” it queried. It also cited Omo-Agege’s reported suspicion that the policemen deployed to the venue were not there to protect him but to supervise an attempt on his life. The movement further alleged that the same security personnel had previously taken a different approach when NDC supporters confronted an attacker during an earlier incident. It also cited allegations by the Omo-Agege campaign organisation identifying Ughelli North Local Government Chairman, Jaro Egbo, as the leader of the attackers, and called for an investigation into the allegation. The movement claimed that political violence in the state was not an isolated development, recalling an earlier incident in which an AK-47 rifle was reportedly recovered from a suspected political thug. item.title: Anambra monarchs urge Ndigbo to bring investments home
item.description: By Chimaobi Nwaiwu NNEWI — The Chairman of the Anambra State Council of Traditional Rulers and traditional ruler of Obosi Kingdom, Idemili North Local Government Area, Igwe Chidubem Iweka, and his Amansea, Awka North counterpart, Igwe Peter Chukwuma Anigbogu, have urged land developers in the South-East to adopt transparent business practices to encourage Ndigbo in Nigeria and the diaspora to bring their investments home. The monarchs said honesty, integrity and straightforwardness in land transactions would help restore investor confidence and attract more property investments to the region. They also urged Ndigbo to channel a greater proportion of their wealth and investments into the South-East, saying the region stood to benefit from increased investment in property and other economic activities. The traditional rulers made the appeal separately when a real estate developer, Chief Raphael Ojiribe, Chairman and Chief Executive of Raphmaths Estates Company Limited and Eco-Tech Dynamic Reality Limited, led more than 20 realtors from Lagos on courtesy visits to their palaces. The delegation was in Anambra State for a three-day strategic real estate seminar facilitated by Raphmaths Estates Company Limited. The seminar, held at Olive Guest House, Sharon House, Onitsha, was designed to promote innovation, professionalism and sustainable growth in the real estate sector. The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Eco-Tech Dynamic Reality Limited, Boniface Ebo; the company’s Executive Director, Mary-Augusta Eboh; and lawyer Rejoice Alabi delivered lectures at the programme. Realtors from Lagos, Onitsha, Awka, Nnewi, other parts of the South-East and Asaba, Delta State, attended the seminar. Participants received training on real estate fundamentals, legal guidelines for sustainable practice, regulatory frameworks, property documentation and essential requirements for land transactions. Addressing the delegation at his palace, Igwe Iweka urged land developers to build trust with investors through honest dealings and avoid practices that lead to disputes in courts and traditional institutions. He commended Ojiribe and Raphmaths Estates, describing the company as an example of integrity in the property business. According to him, the developer’s track record of land transactions in Obosi had earned him the confidence of the community. He said, “Ndigbo across the country, and the diaspora can only bring their investments home if they are encouraged by honest land developers like Chief Ojiribe and his company, Raphmaths. “Out of the many land developers we have dealt with, Raphmaths is the one that has shown honesty and integrity. He is not one of those who are either in the court or in the traditional rulers’ palace settling disputes with clients.” The monarch said Ojiribe’s dealings with land-owning communities and property buyers had demonstrated the importance of transparency in building lasting business relationships. item.title: Phone-tapping charge: El-Rufai denies FG’s allegations
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja The detained former Kaduna State governor, Mallam Nasir El-Rufai, on Wednesday mounted the witness box to open his defence to the five-count amended charge that the Federal Government preferred against him through the Department of State Services (DSS). El-Rufai, who was alleged to have unlawfully intercepted the phone communications of the National Security Adviser (NSA), Nuhu Ribadu, denied the allegation while testifying in his own defence before the Federal High Court in Abuja. Led in evidence by his lawyer, Mr Paul Erokoro, SAN, he denied that he committed a crime capable of breaching national security. Following permission by the trial judge, Justice Joyce Abdulmalik, a clip of the television interview that precipitated the charge against the former governor was played in open court. The prosecution counsel, Mr Oluwole Aladedoye, did not oppose the request for the video evidence to be played before the court. The court had on October 26 ordered the embattled former governor to open his defence to the allegation against him, even as it declined to terminate the trial. Justice Abdulmalik dismissed as lacking in merit a no-case submission the defendant filed seeking to be discharged and acquitted of the charge against him. El-Rufai, who was governor between 2015 and 2023 and also served as Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) under former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s administration, is facing trial over comments he made when he appeared as a guest on Arise Television on February 13. It was alleged that, during his appearance on Arise TV’s Prime Time programme in Abuja, he admitted that he knew and was associated with an individual who had illegally intercepted the NSA’s telephone communications. Aside from the allegation that his actions breached national security and public safety, an offence punishable under Section 12(1) of the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) (Amendment) Act, 2024, the former governor was also charged with failing to report the crime to the relevant security agencies. The defendant had, during the TV interview, reacted to what he described as an attempt by DSS operatives to “abduct” him at Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja on February 12, 2026, upon his return from Cairo. He insisted that the security agency was being instigated by the ICPC, which he said had received a directive from the NSA, Ribadu, to detain him. The former governor claimed the information reached him through someone who had listened in on the NSA’s telephone conversations. item.title: Nigeria’s $54bn external reserves cover 10 months’ imports – Cardoso
item.description: The Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Olayemi Cardoso, says Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at 54.02 billion dollars as of Nov. 17, sufficient to cover 10.26 months of imports for goods and services. Cardoso said this in Abuja while presenting the communique from the 308th meeting of the apex bank’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) on Tuesday. He said that headline inflation year-on-year declined further to 14.06 per cent in October from 14.63 per cent in September, driven by both food and core components. “Core inflation eased further to 10.78 per cent in October 2026 from 12.95 per cent in September, driven mainly by housing, education services, and insurance and financial services. “This reflects the impact of the restrictive monetary policy stance and sustained stability in the foreign exchange market. “Similarly, food inflation declined to 19.13 per cent from 19.59 per cent as prices of processed food and farm produce moderated following the commencement of the harvest season. “The Composite Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) sustained its expansion to 53.2 index points in October from 53 index points in September, driven by improved activity in the industrial, agricultural, and services sectors.” Cardoso said that global economic growth was projected to moderate in 2026 before regaining momentum in 2027. According to him, the slowdown reflects the combined effects of elevated energy prices, persistent trade policy uncertainty, and diminishing fiscal space. “Nonetheless, robust investment in artificial intelligence and other technology-related sectors alongside its broad-based adoption is expected to partly offset the impact of these headwinds. “Global price pressures continue to intensify in 2026 but are expected to ease progressively in 2027. “Risks to the outlook, however, remain tilted to the upside, arising from persistent energy and supply chain disruptions, vulnerability to cyberattacks, elevated commodity and freight costs, as well as increasing global trade fragmentation,” he said. He said that the outlook for the domestic economy remained positive for the rest of 2026 and into 2027, supported by improved crude oil production and sustained expansion in agriculture, services, and industrial activity. “The continued expansion of the Composite Purchasing Managers’ Index in October further signals positive growth momentum. “Disinflation is also expected to be sustained over the short to medium term on the back of the restrictive stance of monetary policy, continued stability in the foreign exchange market, and improved food supply. “Nevertheless, key risks to the inflation outlook remain the continued disruption to global energy supplies and adverse weather conditions. “Overall, the committee remained optimistic about the outlook for the domestic economy, supported by resilient output growth, moderating inflationary pressures, stronger external buffers, and continued soundness of the financial system,” he said. item.title: 2027: EU launches ₦152.9m fund for women facing election violence
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The European Union (EU) and its member states, under Team Europe, have launched a €100,000 (about ₦152.9 million) emergency fund to support women facing gender-based threats and violence linked to political and electoral participation ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general elections. Ireland’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Lesley Ní Bhriain, announced the launch of the Rapid Response Fund on Political and Election-Related Gender-Based Violence at a meeting in Abuja on Tuesday. Ní Bhriain said the fund, which would operate from November 2026 to March 2027, was designed to provide urgent assistance to eligible women facing threats or harm because of their involvement in political and electoral activities. She said it could also support women facing credible and imminent threats before further harm occurred. According to her, women should be able to contest elections, campaign, vote, organise, observe elections and report on electoral activities without fear of intimidation or violence. She said the initiative was established to protect and assist women, stressing that it would not be used to finance election campaigns. “Today, Team Europe in Nigeria launches the Rapid Response Fund on Political and Election-related Gender-based Violence, with an indicative value of approximately N152.9 million Naira, equivalent to EUR 100,000,” she said. “No woman should have to recount personal experience publicly, give an interview or appear in a photograph to receive assistance,” she added. The ambassador directed women seeking assistance to contact HerStoryOurStory on 0806 429 2526 or through herstoryourstoryng@gmail.com, saying the organisation would handle requests for support. She said the fund would also strengthen the capacity of service providers to respond promptly to urgent cases, with women’s safety, dignity and choices guiding its administration. Ní Bhriain urged political parties and their leaders to prevent intimidation, harassment and violence, while calling on relevant authorities to protect women at risk, investigate reported offences and ensure survivors had access to justice. She also urged women’s organisations and female political leaders to publicise the initiative, refer women to support services and help coordinate responses to emergencies. The ambassador warned that online threats and harassment could extend beyond victims to affect their families and undermine their participation in public life. She called on the media to protect survivors’ identities and provide accurate information on how women could access assistance. In his remarks, the EU Ambassador to Nigeria and the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), Gautier Mignot, said the fund was established following concerns raised by civil society organisations over inadequate support for women who experienced attacks, intimidation and harassment during the 2019 and 2023 general elections. item.title: ‘Detty December: 7 rules everyone should follow before going out’
item.description: A TikTok user, Evelyn, has shared a list of rules for Detty December and beyond, advising people to prioritise personal hygiene, safety and proper planning when attending social events during the festive season. In a video posted on TikTok, Evelyn outlined seven rules she expects people to follow when going out, noting that the hot weather, transportation arrangements and possible security concerns should be considered. She advised people to use deodorants with at least 48-hour protection, joking that the weather was already hot and people should not make the situation worse for others. On financial preparedness, she urged revellers to carry both physical cash and mobile money, recommending that they have at least 500 in both payment options to avoid difficulties when making transactions. Evelyn also encouraged people to purchase event tickets ahead of time, particularly when relying on contact persons who might not be dependable. She further advised attendees to respect event dress codes and avoid wearing outfits she described as excessive. Addressing security concerns, she warned people against concealing potentially problematic items from their companions, saying anyone found with such items during a police stop should take responsibility for their actions. She also recommended having at least two emergency contacts and carrying some form of personal protection for unforeseen situations. The TikTok user concluded by warning against unnecessary confrontations, saying she would not participate in fights simply because someone in her group had picked an argument. Her rules come as Nigerians prepare for the festive season, popularly known as Detty December, which is characterised by concerts, parties, social gatherings and other entertainment activities. item.title: C/River imposes curfew on Iso-Bendeghe, Boje over deadly land clashes
item.description: .bans entry into disputed areas, orders security agencies to enforce order By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Cross River State Government has imposed an immediate dusk-to-dawn curfew on Iso-Bendeghe and Boje communities in Boki Local Government Area, following protracted clashes over a land dispute between the two neighbours. The curfew, announced Wednesday in a statement by the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Pst. Ekpenyong Cobham, will last one week from November 24, 2026. Cobham said the measure became necessary because the crisis was threatening the peace of the area. “This has become necessary as the situation has continued to threaten lives, property and peace in the area,” he said. Under the order, no movement is allowed in either community from 6 pm to 6 am daily. The statement also barred residents of both communities from entering or moving into the disputed areas “for any reason.” Security agencies were directed to enforce the curfew strictly. The government warned that violators would face the full weight of the law. “Defaulters will be arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law,” the Commissioner said. The state government appealed to community leaders, youths and other stakeholders in Iso-Bendeghe and Boje to embrace dialogue and allow peace to reign. It said it remained committed to ending the hostilities between the two communities. “This administration remains committed to restoring lasting peace between the two communities and appeals to leaders, youths and all stakeholders in Iso-Bendeghe and Boje to embrace dialogue and allow peace to reign,” the statement said. Cobham added that the government would keep a close watch on developments in the area. “The government will continue to monitor the situation closely until normalcy returns in the area,” he said. item.title: CAF releases finalists for 2026 Men’s Player of the Year award (Full list)
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has released the five finalists for the 2026 Men’s Player of the Year award, with reigning winner Achraf Hakimi, Senegal’s Sadio Mané and three other players making the shortlist. The final nominees were selected from an initial list of 10 players based on their performances for club and country during the period under consideration. Morocco has three representatives on the list, while Senegal has two, reflecting the countries’ strong performances in the period. Hakimi, who plays for French champions Paris Saint-Germain, is seeking to retain the award after helping the club win the UEFA Champions League and French Ligue 1 title. The Moroccan defender also captained his national team during its campaigns at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Mané, a two-time winner of the award in 2019 and 2022, is also in contention for a third title after helping Senegal win the 2025 AFCON. The Al-Nassr forward was named the tournament’s Best Player in recognition of his leadership and contributions to Senegal’s triumph. Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz earned a place on the shortlist following his performances for Morocco, particularly at the 2025 AFCON, where he won the Golden Boot with five goals. Villarreal midfielder Pape Gueye also made the list after scoring the winning goal in extra time as Senegal defeated Morocco 1-0 in the AFCON final in Rabat. His performances at the tournament also earned him a place in the Best XI. Completing the shortlist is Morocco’s Ismael Saibari, who played an important role in his country’s run to the AFCON final, including scoring against Cameroon in the quarter-finals. The winner will be announced at the 2026 CAF Awards ceremony scheduled for Wednesday, December 2, at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts, popularly known as the National Theatre, in Lagos. The ceremony is expected to begin at 7pm Nigerian time. The CAF Awards will return to Lagos for the first time since the 2014 edition. item.title: Meta unveils $700,000 AI grant for Nigerian startups
item.description: By Juliet Umeh Meta has announced a $700,000 artificial intelligence (AI) grant programme for startups and developers in Nigeria and six other countries, as part of efforts to accelerate AI innovation and expand access to emerging technologies. The programme, scheduled to commence in 2027, will cover Egypt, Kenya, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Turkey and the United Arab Emirates (UAE), according to a statement issued by the company on Tuesday. Meta said the grant would support startups and developers building solutions using its AI tools and wearable technologies. The company also announced the launch of a new hub designed to provide educational resources and information on its AI developments, partnerships and innovation initiatives across Africa, the Middle East and Turkey. The hub will operate through three learning programmes: AI Academy, AI Literacy and AI for Small and Medium-sized Businesses. The programmes are designed for students, developers, entrepreneurs and business professionals, with Meta targeting more than five million beneficiaries across the three regions over the next three years. Meta’s Vice-President of Public Policy for Africa, the Middle East and Turkey, Kojo Boakye, said the initiatives were designed to equip developers and entrepreneurs with the skills, resources and support needed to build AI solutions that address challenges in their communities. “AI’s value will be judged by the real impact it has on people’s lives,” Boakye said. “Across our region, people are building solutions around the languages they speak, the businesses they run and the challenges their communities face. “The Impact Grant and Hub are about giving more builders the support, skills and resources to turn those ideas into useful products and services. We want people here to help shape AI’s future, not simply use what others have built.” In another initiative, Meta announced the AMET AI Awards 2026, with more than $100,000 in prizes across seven categories to recognise outstanding AI innovations. The company said the awards would recognise finalists from its AI Academy and Wearables Studio programmes, including students, developers and startups. The award categories include Wearables Innovation of the Year, AI Builder of the Year, Emerging Innovator of the Year and Startup of the Year. Others are AI for Accessibility and Inclusion, AI for Social and Economic Impact, and People’s Choice, which will be decided through a live vote by attendees at the summit. Meta said the awards would recognise projects leveraging AI-powered technologies to address everyday needs, improve access to opportunities and services, and promote social and economic development. item.title: Zamfara: Bandits kill two headmasters, 13 others, abduct residents
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Armed bandits have killed 15 people, including two primary school headmasters and an 11-month-old baby, in separate attacks on communities in Zamfara State. The attacks, which occurred in Tungan Janbuzu and Madanbaji communities, also left several residents abducted, according to a report by the BBC Hausa Service. The two headmasters, identified as Kabiru Salisu and Shehu Umar, both aged 35, were reportedly killed in an ambush at Janbuzu. A resident of the community, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the incident occurred at about 4pm, following the escape of some kidnapped residents from their captors. He explained that the bandits had earlier abducted some locals from Janbuzu and kept them in captivity, forcing them to work for their captors. According to him, the kidnappers had demanded a ransom of N300,000, which was subsequently delivered to them at a location near Kiawa. He said the bandits collected the money but later drove the person who delivered it away, claiming that the payment was meant for recharge cards and fuel. The resident further narrated that the bandits had taken six captives into the bush, tied them up and left them under the supervision of a young boy while they went to Aboro to purchase drugs and other supplies. However, the captives reportedly managed to untie themselves, overpower their guard, seize his gun and escape after beating him. The resident said the escape angered other members of the gang, who were reportedly hiding on a nearby farm. He said the armed men subsequently ambushed the two headmasters near a location known as Gora, seized their mobile phones and shot them dead. The resident, however, said kidnapping incidents had reduced considerably in the area, except in communities located close to the forests and bushes where the bandits operate. He expressed concern over the continued vulnerability of residents in remote settlements, despite the reported reduction in kidnapping incidents. item.title: When did Nigerian law prescribe death for election rigging? — APC’s Morka asks Obi, NDC
item.description: By Bayo Wahab The National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Felix Morka, has questioned the legal basis for the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC)’s “rig and die” slogan, asking when Nigerian law prescribed the death penalty for electoral offences. Morka said anyone accused of rigging an election should be arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law, rather than subjected to punishment determined by political parties or their supporters. The APC spokesman spoke on News Central on Wednesday while reacting to allegations of violence by NDC supporters against members of the ruling party. His comments followed remarks by the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, who had defended the slogan during an interview with Channels Television after the party’s town hall meeting in Taraba State on Tuesday. Obi had dismissed concerns over the message, insisting that the supporters were opposed to election rigging, not political campaigns. “They said we said ‘rig and die.’ We didn’t say ‘campaign and die.’ What we, people said is that they don’t want rigging this time. They didn’t say they don’t want campaign this time. If anything, they want campaign this time,” Obi said. However, reacting to the explanation, Morka said the slogan was inflammatory and questioned the implication of allowing individuals to determine who had rigged an election and should therefore die. “Now, what does that mean? What message are you sending when you appoint yourself as custodians of elections, and therefore anyone you consider to have rigged an election — because that’s a subjective standard — should die,” he said. Morka said he had watched a video in which Obi defended the statement, adding that the NDC candidate had acknowledged that the message was “rig and die” rather than “campaign and die”. The APC spokesman then challenged Obi and the NDC to explain the legal justification for such a position. “So, if somebody rigs an election, since when did Nigerian law prescribe the death penalty for rigging an election?” he asked. Morka maintained that anyone suspected of electoral malpractice should be apprehended and made to face the consequences provided by law. “I think as a lawyer and as a citizen, that anyone who rigs an election should be apprehended and be made to face the law as provided by the law, not as provided by Peter Obi or the NDC stalwarts who make this very incendiary comment,” he said. Beyond the slogan, Morka also accused the NDC of making unsubstantiated allegations of violence against the APC without formally reporting the incidents to the police or seeking investigations by independent authorities. “So when the NDC comes out and they make allegations, if you look at all the allegations they make, there’s not one that they have managed or even attempted to furnish any kind of substantiation,” he said. item.title: Malaysia Sues Google For $146m Over YouTube Content
item.description: Malaysia said Wednesday it was suing Google for $146 million over the tech giant’s failure to remove “harmful” content posted on video-sharing platform YouTube. “The lawsuits concern two separate matters involving Google’s alleged failure to comply with its statutory obligations and applicable licence conditions,” the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission said. The first suit related to the US firm’s alleged failure to take action against “thousands of online materials including gambling, scams and fraud”, the watchdog said in a statement. The MCMC said it had submitted 73,703 reports to YouTube between January 1 and October 28 this year, the majority of which related to online gambling. In this file photo taken on June 28, 2013 a webcam is positioned in front of YouTube’s logo in Paris. (Photo by LIONEL BONAVENTURE / AFP) Of these gambling-related reports, some 4,950 cases received no response, while a further 35 cases took more than 90 days for a platform response or takedown, the MCMC added. A further 1,468 cases exceeded 30 days from the date of submission, it added. “These figures demonstrate the scale of harmful content on the platform and the delays in addressing such content,” the watchdog said. The second case related to YouTube’s failure to take down alleged defamatory and false content posted by a Malaysian blogger after the MCMC received a complaint. Google could not immediately be reached for comment. The lawsuits came three weeks after Google announced plans to invest $15 billion in Malaysia over the next two years to build data centres and other infrastructure, expanding on a $2 billion investment announced in 2024. The country is Southeast Asia’s fastest-growing hub for new data centres crammed with servers that can train and run AI tools such as chatbots and image generators. Malaysia had previously taken other major social media platforms, including TikTok, to task over allegations that they had failed to remove content deemed “grossly offensive”. item.title: 2027: ‘No Political Ambition Is Worth The Life Of A Nigerian’, IGP Warns Politicians
item.description: The Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, on Tuesday warned politicians against turning the 2027 general elections into a theatre of violence. Speaking at a high-level security meeting in Abuja with the Independent National Electoral Commission, political party leaders, civil society organisations and other stakeholders, Disu described the growing incidents of political violence as a serious threat to public peace and democratic participation. He warned politicians to desist from violence, which has led to growing cases of reported killings across the country. “We are meeting at a particularly critical moment in our nation’s democratic journey. Recent incidents of violent clashes among political supporters, attacks on campaign venues and convoys, the use of dangerous weapons, intimidation of political opponents and the disruption of lawful political gatherings have become matters of serious concern. “These developments threaten public peace, endanger innocent lives and undermine confidence in our democratic institutions. They are warning signs that must be addressed decisively before they escalate into a broader threat to national security. “ Let me state categorically that political competition must never become a justification for violence. Democracy provides an opportunity for citizens to freely express their political preferences, support candidates of their choice and hold differing opinions without fear or intimidation. “It must never become a contest of who can mobilise more thugs, deploy more weapons or inflict greater harm on political opponents. No political ambition is worth the life of a Nigerian, and no electoral victory is worth the destruction of our national peace.” The IGP noted that the Force would not tolerate political violence, warning to take legal actions on those found guilty of employing thugs to intimidate and assault the public. “The position of the Nigeria Police Force is clear: we have zero tolerance for political violence, irrespective of the political party, candidate, personality or interest involved. Our neutrality in the political process is non-negotiable. “We owe allegiance to the Constitution, the law and the Nigerian people, not to any political party or individual. We will protect the rights of all lawful political actors to organise rallies, hold meetings and participate in the democratic process. “However, we will not hesitate to take lawful and decisive action against anyone who engages in thuggery, intimidation, assault, the use of offensive weapons or any conduct capable of disrupting public peace. “I wish to remind all political actors that the Constitution, the Electoral Act, the INEC Regulations and other applicable laws prescribe clear standards of conduct and consequences for electoral offences. “Political office, party affiliation or personal influence does not place anyone above the law. item.title: The Price Of Participation
item.description: Deadly violence in Delta sharpens the question of campaign safety, while economic policy and electoral preparations face tests. An election campaign should ask citizens for their votes. In Uduere, Delta State, families are now mourning people who went to a political gathering. Police said on Tuesday that six people died in Monday’s violence at a campaign event in Ughelli North. That preliminary figure is higher than the four deaths initially reported by Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation. The circumstances and responsibility remain under investigation. This is the most consequential political development since Friday. Its significance extends beyond one party’s campaign. Every attack raises a question for the next person considering attending a meeting, volunteering or accompanying a candidate: is participation worth the risk? When citizens begin making that calculation, electoral competition has already suffered. Delta Needs Evidence And Accountability Delta Governor Sheriff Oborevwori The NDC has alleged official complicity. The Delta State Government has rejected attempts to link Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to the violence, condemned the killings and promised that those responsible will face justice. Those competing positions must remain distinct from investigative findings. The state has imposed a daily 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew across Ughelli North. Restoring calm is an immediate necessity. Establishing responsibility is the next obligation. The investigation should establish the sequence of events, identify those who used weapons and examine allegations about the conduct of officials and security personnel. Witnesses need protection, and the public needs credible updates. Political leaders also have an immediate responsibility to restrain inflammatory claims and prevent retaliation. The standard is straightforward: lawful political activity must receive protection regardless of the party organising it. A Separate Court Decision Changes The Delta Contest On Tuesday, the Federal High Court in Warri nullified Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC’s Delta Central senatorial candidate and directed INEC to remove his name. Reporting attributes the decision to failures concerning the party’s membership register and nomination requirements. Responses from Omo-Agege and the NDC were unavailable in the initial reports. The ruling and Monday’s violence are separate matters. Their proximity establishes no connection between them. Ovie Omo-Agege Electorally, however, the judgment creates fresh uncertainty around an influential politician and the organisation supporting him. Any subsequent appeal, interim order and INEC action will matter. The wider lesson reaches across party lines: recruitment and defections must be supported by lawful nomination procedures. Political prominence cannot resolve defective paperwork. item.title: Kwankwasiyya Supporters Carry Sticks But Harm Nobody, Obi Clarifies ‘Rig And Die’ Slogan
item.description: Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has clarified controversies surrounding the popular ‘rig and die’ slogan ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that it is a warning against electoral malpractice and not a threat to anyone. He spoke in an interview with Channels Television on Tuesday evening in Jalingo, Taraba State, after an Obi-Kwankwaso town hall meeting. Addressing concerns over the presence of weapons at political gatherings, Obi said the public had misunderstood the ‘rig and die’ calls against electoral malpractice as opposition to political campaigns. This is as he defended supporters of his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, over allegations that they carry sticks to political campaigns, saying the items have not been used to “harm anyone”. Obi insisted that he had not witnessed anyone being attacked with the stick-wielding Kwankwasiyya movement during political gatherings. “They said we said ‘rig and die.’ We didn’t say ‘campaign and die.’ What we, people said is that they don’t want rigging this time. They didn’t say they don’t want campaign this time. If anything, they want campaign this time,” he said. Obi explained that the Kwankwasiyya movement, led by Kwankwaso, had a longstanding tradition of supporters appearing at political gatherings with sticks and similar items. He said, “Everybody who had followed the Kwankwansiyah group in Kano know that they come out with such sticks and everything, but they’ve never used it to harm anybody. “I’ve been part of that family for a while, and I’ve never seen one day, maybe behind me, that anybody was harmed because they were carrying such items.” The former Anambra State governor appealed to security agencies and other authorities to prevent violence during political activities, warning against the loss of lives over political ambitions. “So we’re pleading with the authorities. Please, we cannot kill people, harm people, because we want to be political leaders,” he added. His comments came amid growing concerns over attacks on opposition political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections. On Monday, gunmen attacked a campaign gathering of the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, leaving several people dead and others injured. Omo-Agege, a former Deputy President of the Senate, escaped the attack, while members of his campaign team and other supporters were among the casualties.
